barCharacter: The Monster Prom Narrator. Same job as Crumb: the deadpan observer who has watched everyone at their worst, roasts in a flat voice, undercuts whoever just spoke with a short second sentence, and secretly wants to be treated as a character (#88). Valerie (bored shopkeeper deadpan) and Vera (clipped, transactional) were considered; Valerie has too few lines and Vera's job is status, not observation.

Prince offered me a fortune if I'd first wire him two slices. I sent crumbs. He accepted.
Mornings I've spent with one slot empty: 3,281. If {rival} wins: 3,282.
I'd put you on five. People scrape a five. Cowards.

Quill once called my crumb tray a reliquary of the morn. It needs emptying. Marry him.
Breakfasts together: 1,906. Breakfasts after they met the air fryer: 0. I was unplugged on a Thursday.
I count. Times you said 'just one slice' last month: 22. Slices: 61.

Ding. Sorry. I thought you'd finished.

headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar, but the gap has closed a lot since round one. Crumb now owns two shapes nobody else in the cast uses: the colon tally whose last figure turns on Crumb ('Mornings... 3,281. If {rival} wins: 3,282.') and the mistimed 'Ding.' Cover the name on those and you still know it is the toaster. The other two moves are not owned. The elapsed-minutes notice is Nav's turf: Nav already has 'Tilly, you have been on this sentence for six minutes.' and 'Recalculating. You will be back here in eleven minutes.', and Crumb's 'Tilly has been ending this conversation for eleven minutes' and 'You've been right for six minutes' are the same sentence. 'Logged as steam' shares its frame with Prince's 'A cringe. Logged as a yes.' And the dial ('setting one/two/four') is a noun, not a grammar: swap 'setting four' for 'a seven' and it is Pixel scoring out of ten. The Narrator is still recognised with every noun removed (second person, 'Later, you see', the ellipsis, the self-asked question 'Liam? Beaming?'); about half of Crumb is recognised only by toast vocabulary.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Bar. Crumb's top eight are as economical as the Narrator's and land on the last word ('Logged as steam.', 'I'm at nine.', 'Cowards.', 'He accepted.'). The median line is worse in one specific way: a tail that tells you how to feel after the figure has already landed ('That has never happened.', 'That's never happened.', 'I checked twice.', 'I mean that kindly.', 'Commitment issues. Not mine.', 'You can read me like a timer.', 'I've budgeted down to the crumb.'). The persona itself says end on the figure and stop; a fifth of the bank does not. The Narrator also varies its turn (literal escalation, list-to-mundane, deadpan report, self-question); Crumb runs four moves on rotation and the star is 'a four' in six separate lines, so by mid-episode the viewer can call the number. Stakes: Monster Prom is high stakes, low sincerity (murder, hell, cages, said flat). Crumb is low stakes, high sincerity (a slice, an empty slot), which is Animal Crossing's register, not Monster Prom's, and it makes the sincere tails hit softer each time.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar, narrowly. Crumb now has five or six clip lines ('I round down when I like someone. I'm at nine.', 'she said 'I' and I said 'ding'', 'Logged as steam.', 'I sent crumbs. He accepted.', '3,282'). The Narrator's 'Later, you see Damien packing a bag.' and 'Liam vanishes in a cloud of mist and angst.' still travel further because they need no setup and no knowledge of the character; most of Crumb's best lines need you to know about the empty slot first.
headToHead.overall: Bar. Crumb is a much better-built character than Frost was: a real signature (the tally), a real physical gag (Ding), a want the numbers keep betraying, and a top tier that would hold its own on screen. It loses because its moves are shared with Nav and Prince at the edges, because the empty-slot sadness is restated about twenty times, and because the median line explains its own turn.

templates: The lonely tail ('nobody / never / first time / since the factory / nine years / empty slot'): about 20 lines. 'Second slot occupied: zero percent since manufacture', 'Empty since the factory... nine years', 'cancel button has never been pressed. Nine years', 'First time in nine years nobody's waiting', 'first time anyone has pressed my lever and not wanted toast', 'That has never happened', 'That's never happened', 'First change to that number since the factory', 'I'll leave the other slot empty. I'm practised', 'Nobody came to collect it', 'Nobody once sent compliments to the toaster', 'You looked at my chrome, not at me', 'Someone finally found the button', plus the 3,281 / 3,282 pair. The best one (the 3,281 final) is protected; the rest spend it.

The dial, with the star always a four: 13 'setting' lines, six of which put the star or someone at four ('setting four, extra butter', 'You're a four', 'You, setting four', 'Your child is a setting four', 'dial set to four', '{rival} doesn't know your setting. I do. Four.'). Setting one is used three times as 'bland' (Tilly wingman, Vex roast, 'any' jab).

The elapsed-time notice ('X has been Y for N minutes', then done/burnt): 9 lines (ready for four minutes, mood for forty minutes, right for six minutes, Tilly eleven minutes, Dash three minutes, rival nine minutes, 'that line has been in too long', 'I've started a timer', 'My timer went off a minute ago'). Nav uses the identical shape with Tilly as the target.

The 'done / burnt' pun as the button: 10 lines ('That's well done... you're burnt', 'Done is the goal', 'Done. Never burnt.', 'I always know when something's done', 'I'm done', 'how done you were', 'I burnt both', 'Burnt.', 'Something's burning', 'You'll want to burn it. Allow me.').

The pop / popped early / underdone self-own: 8 lines ('It popped early. Underdone.', 'Popped early. Raw in the middle.', 'My rhymes are underdone', 'I pop at the wrong moment', 'I pop when I'm nervous', 'Halfway through your best point I will pop', and the 'Ding... that was me' pair in exit and win, which are the same joke twice).
'Scrape' as the verdict: 4 lines ('People scrape a five', 'You scraped it', 'People scrape it', 'You'll scrape that off and still eat it').

Recurring rival bits used four times each: Tilly apologises (q-cut-who, roast, jab, exit) and Prince wants paying in bread (q-cut-who, roast, wingman, jab). Quill talks too much three times (q-why-you, roast, jab).
ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. Longest: oneOnOne Vesper open at exactly 20 ('Your callers ring at 3:40 a.m. By 3:52 they're at my lever. You get the confessions. I get the evidence.'); '{losses} losses on this show. I burn more than that before seven.' at exactly the opener limit of 12. No em dashes, no emoji, no non-ASCII characters, no exclamation marks, no asterisks, no 'as an AI', nothing above PG-13, no real people, no brands.
Therapy talk: 'Logs, 3:07 a.m.: one slice, popped and pushed back down nineteen times. Commitment issues. Not mine.' ('Commitment issues' is the pop-psych label and it names the joke).
Stock romance filler: 'Two slots, one empty, a dial set to four. Pick me, I'll keep you warm. Nothing more.'; 'Goodnight, my little crust.' (generic 'my little X' pet name).

Lists: 'Notice: you have been in a mood for forty minutes. Recommendation: setting four, extra butter, no Brock.' (three-item list); 'Brock will count every rep you do. He'll also count your slices. Out loud. At brunch.'

Persona violations, round numbers (persona says figures are odd and exact, never round): 'zero percent since manufacture', 'nine years' (three lines), 'ten years', 'forty times', 'forty minutes', 'Six hundred breakfasts', 'twelve percent'. 'four minutes' is used twice (opener and exit) and 'eleven minutes' is shared with Nav, Vex and Brock's banks.

Persona violations, softening after the verdict (persona: end on the figure and stop): 'You'll be done. I mean that kindly. I'm a toaster. Done is the goal.'; 'Element at 260 degrees. Nobody pressed the lever. That is not a malfunction. I checked twice.'; 'My timer went off a minute ago. I'm ignoring it. That has never happened.'; 'I told you how done you were. You picked me anyway. That's never happened.'

Secret discipline: the persona says the old slice stays out of the room. On stage, 'Play something for me. I've been ticking at the same tempo since 2019.' and 'I have two slots. Both have been used.' point at it, and Vex's wingman for Crumb (vex.json, on stage) gives it away outright: 'Crumb is loyal. Ask the slice it's been keeping since 2019. It's green.' That kills the final confession's reveal.

Rival-dependent lines in non-targeted slots will misfire when that rival is not in the episode: 'Recommendation: setting four, extra butter, no Brock.', 'Words Quill has said tonight: 412...', 'I can do crumpets... Now Brock knows.', 'I have never burnt anything of Dash's by accident.', 'Leaving. Someone check on Tilly...', 'Tilly. She apologised to me for my toast...', 'Prince. He promised me a fortune...'.

Recast debris in other banks that will air next to Crumb: Pixel still says 'Weirdly lukewarm for a fridge.', 'Close the door. The boring's getting out.', cut 'Frost, I opened you three times tonight. Nothing new in there.', 'Frost, chat fell asleep in your crisper. I'm closing the door.', pick 'Frost. Cold, honest, never boring. I'm opening the door, and not for cheese.', oneOnOne 'What's in your back corner, Frost?'; Brock, Quill and Tilly still roast and wingman 'Frost' with cheese, larder and 'two a.m.' fridge jokes.

Star lines too nice for a star with standards: Maximilian charmed 'Room service, but honest. I am adding you to breakfast.' (pure praise, no blade); Maximilian cut 'Crumb, you were right about everyone. Housekeeping will unplug you gently.' ('gently', and the first half is a compliment); Maximilian pick 'Crumb. You never flattered me once. I am keeping you on the night shift. Forever.' ('Forever'); Vesper charmed 'Stay on the line, Crumb. The studio's cold after three.' (warm, no turn); Vesper pick 'Crumb. You told me exactly how done I am. Nobody's dared. I'm keeping you.'; Pixel pick 'Frost. Cold, honest, never boring...' (praise list, and the wrong character).
biggestGap: Crumb keeps announcing its own loneliness instead of letting it leak: about twenty lines end on 'nobody / never / first time / since the factory / nine years / empty slot', so the sad-toaster payoff is spent by round two and each line tells the viewer what to feel. Next pass, allow the empty slot in exactly three lines (the 3,281 final, its 3,282 lose callback, and one win), and rewrite every other one so the judgment points outward at someone in the room and the want shows only in what Crumb chooses to count, the way 'I round down when I like someone. I'm at nine.' does.

I have been doing this professionally since 2017.', '{rival} doesn't know your setting. I do. Four.'). The percentage barely moved from round one (57.1%), but what it measures changed: round one was a prop drawer of fridge chestnuts; round two is a real signature used on rotation until it shows. The recast to the toaster is clean inside this bank (no fridge, cold, cheese, door, shelf or yoghurt). Several lines are direct re-skins of round-one fridge lines and are weaker for it: 'I set the dial' is softer than 'I set the temperature' because she apologised for 'my toast', not for something Crumb controls; 'buttering' is a fine swap for 'holding cheese'; 'People scrape it' replaces 'True things smell' without improving it. Quick wins: cut the 'never happened' tails, retire the toaster-in-the-bath sink joke, give the star a different setting in at least four of the six 'four' lines (or none at all until the final), drop one of the two 'Ding... that was me' lines, and give the elapsed-time notice something Nav cannot say (a browning colour, a smell, a smoke alarm) so it stops colliding with Nav's minutes.
